This deliverable is a scope guard that keeps known out-of-scope and retired items visible so they are not accidentally reintroduced via implementation enthusiasm, runtime event logging, release packaging, plugin/tool expansion, SDK settings behavior, or future domain-engine work.
The controlling objective is OBJ-009: preserve professional boundary, product identity, and reliance-boundary ownership in docs, UI, runtime, and release behavior.
Principle: treat boundary rows as negative scope controls, not implementation backlog.

Principle: a future-facing statement is not current shipping scope; domain-engine profiles, plugin-like extension points, and remote MCP may be described as future-compatible but implementation requires amendment and mature local governance first.
Principle: runtime event logging is allowed runtime infrastructure but does not revive retired pipeline hardening work (PLAN §9; PRD §3.2).
Principle: shipped safety posture cannot depend on SDK defaults, ambient user settings, ordinary bypass behavior, or prompt text alone (CONTRACT §1.4 K-SDK-1, §1.6 K-PERM-2/3/6).
Principle: human authority remains non-delegable; the register can guide amendment and review but cannot approve professional work or create reliance by itself.
Boundary-row placement guidance: inspect the concrete boundary rows in Datasheet.md under Boundary Register Rows, the current register-row artifact unless a governed publication step moves them.

Keep remote MCP and plugins out of current scope until local/in-process SDK integration, permission policy, hooks, event logging, and result storage are stable and a governed amendment permits expansion.
Broad tool search is deferred; if later introduced it must reveal only currently allowed tools and never denied tools (PRD §8.14 FR-103).
Do not allow shipped builds to load ambient Claude settings; a change attempt should trigger governance review before implementation.
Separate developer-local guarded bypass from shipped or ordinary operator workflows; do not blur this distinction in copy, config, or tests.
Keep retired PKG-08 items (execution-root validator, dependency graph generator, deliverable lock, unified pipeline run record, staleness propagation tooling) out of current commitments.
Treat macOS 15+ Apple Silicon DMG as the current release target; Windows/Linux packaging needs amendment.
Keep domain operation execution behind future profile, proposal, deterministic checks, and human acceptance (CONTRACT §1.10; PRD R7).

Trade-off future compatibility vs current scope discipline: preserve future vocabulary but mark implementation as future-amendment scope to prevent premature implementation while keeping architectural runway.
Trade-off developer convenience vs shipped safety: allow only guarded developer-local bypass and forbid shipped/ordinary bypass behavior to maintain product-owned permission boundaries.
Trade-off event logging vs retired pipeline scope: permit runtime audit event logging but keep retired pipeline run records and hardening tools retired.
Trade-off cross-platform ambition vs release certainty: keep Windows/Linux packaging out of current scope because the release invariant names macOS 15+ Apple Silicon DMG unless amended.
